transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I came in because most days I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling in my chest. It’s hard to explain. I used to be Ruben, you know, the guy who could talk to anybody—customers, neighbors, whoever—and actually enjoy the day. That was kind of my thing in sales, being able to chat with people.

Lately it feels like that old version of me is just… gone. Like I’m there, but not really there.
How long have you been feeling this way?

About eight months, I think. It started around when the new regional manager came in and started really riding me… taking accounts I’d had for years. I mean, those were people I knew, not just names on a spreadsheet. Anyway, yeah—about eight months.
Do you still find pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy?

Not really, no. I mean, I used to look forward to bowling night, messing around in the garden, taking my wife to those little gallery shows she likes… we even used to go dancing sometimes, back when my knees weren’t the whole conversation. 

Now when something comes up, I just sort of sit there and think of reasons not to go. I tell her I’m tired, or maybe next time, or the yard can wait… but honestly, none of it feels worth the effort anymore.
Have you ever thought about ending your life during these past eight months?

Yeah… I have. I don’t like saying that out loud.

It’s not like I’m sitting there making some big speech about it, but I’ll wake up sometimes and think… maybe my wife and the kids would be better off if I just didn’t wake up. And then I feel ashamed for even thinking that, because my wife—she’s put up with me through a lot, you know, even back when I’d come home talking too much about work and she’d just nod along like she understood all the customer drama.

But yeah… those thoughts have been there. And they scare me, honestly. I don’t trust myself the way I used to.
Have you had any periods where you felt better, almost back to normal, during these past eight months?

No… not really back to normal. It’s been pretty much this whole stretch, about eight months now, since that new regional manager came in and started coming down on me. 

I mean, at first I kept thinking it was just a rough week, you know? Sales has rough weeks. I’ve had managers before who thought yelling was leadership. But then he started taking accounts I’d handled for years, people I’d built up relationships with… and it just never really lifted after that. Maybe I’ve had a decent afternoon here or there, but not like I felt like myself again.
Have you had any periods, no matter how brief, where you felt completely free of these depressed feelings during the past eight months?

Completely free of it? No… I don’t think so. It’s been hanging around the whole time, about eight months now.

It really started after that new regional manager came in and started riding me all the time—taking away accounts I’d had for years, people I knew by name, knew their kids’ names sometimes. I know that sounds like work stuff, but… it just all seemed to start there and it hasn’t really let up since.
Have you had more than one episode of feeling this way in your life, before these past eight months?

I don’t know… I mean, everybody has bad stretches, right? I’ve had rough times before, sure. Sales’ll do that to you—one month you’re everyone’s favorite guy, next month you can’t get someone to return a call, and you start taking it home with you.

But feeling like this? For this long? I’m not sure. I can’t really remember another time where it was… the same as this. Maybe I’m not answering that right.
Have you ever felt this low or depressed before in your life, prior to these past eight months?

I mean… I’ve been down before, sure. Everybody has, I guess. But this kind of low… waking up most days with this heavy, hollow feeling in my chest, like the old Ruben—the guy who could talk to anybody, joke with clients, enjoy a day—like he’s just gone… I don’t remember feeling that before these last months.

It’s strange, because I used to be the guy people would send into a room when things were tense, you know? I could smooth things over. Now I wake up and it’s like there’s nothing there to reach for. So no, not like this.
Have you had more than one episode of feeling depressed like this before in your life?

No, I don’t think there’s been more than one like this. I mean, I’ve had bad days before—everybody does, especially in sales, you know, one bad call can ruin your whole afternoon—but this is different.

This time I came in because most days I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling in my chest, like the old Ruben… the one who could talk to anybody and actually enjoy his day… like he’s just gone. I don’t remember another time in my life where it felt like that.
Have you experienced any periods of significant depression before this 8-month period?

I don’t think so… not significant like this. I mean, I’ve had stretches where work was terrible or I felt kind of beat up by life, and I’d go home and complain, maybe snap at people, that kind of thing.

But before these eight months? I can’t point to a time and say, yeah, that was the same thing. My memory’s not perfect, you know—after 58 years everything kind of blends together, jobs, bills, kids growing up, all of it—but no, I don’t think I had a period like this before.
Have you had any other episodes of depression in your life that lasted for more than two weeks?

More than two weeks… I don’t know, I don’t think so. I mean, life has had its rough patches, sure—when work was slow, or when money got tight, you kind of carry it around for a while. In sales, you can have a bad month and start thinking the whole world’s against you.

But an actual episode like this, lasting weeks? I can’t really point to one. Not that I remember.
Have you had any episodes of depression before this one that a doctor or therapist diagnosed as depression?

No… not that I know of. I’ve never had a doctor or therapist sit me down and say, “This is depression,” before this.

I mean, I haven’t exactly been the kind of guy who runs to appointments for every little thing—my wife used to get on me about that, saying I’d rather complain about something for six months than make a phone call. And with work, you just kind of keep going, you know? Sales doesn’t really care if you’re having a rough time.

But no, as far as an actual diagnosis from somebody, I don’t have anything like that before now.
Have you had any episodes of depression before this one that felt similar to what you're experiencing now?

No, not really… I mean, I’ve been down before, sure. Everybody has, right? You have a bad quarter, boss is breathing down your neck, car needs work, suddenly the dishwasher goes too—those kinds of things pile up.

But similar to this? I don’t think so. This feels different enough that I would’ve remembered it, I think. My wife probably would’ve remembered too, she was always better at keeping track of what was going on with me than I was. But no, I can’t really think of an earlier time that felt like this.
Have you had any episodes of depression before this one that a mental health professional treated?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I never really had someone in that field treat me for this before.

I’ve talked to people about stress here and there—well, not professionals, more like coworkers over coffee or my wife when she’d catch me staring at bills at the kitchen table. She always said I’d talk in circles before I’d just say what was bothering me. But as far as a counselor or psychiatrist actually treating me for depression before this… no, I don’t have anything like that.
Have you had any other episodes of depression in your life that were treated by a mental health professional?

No… I mean, not by a mental health professional, no. I never really had that kind of treatment before.

I guess looking back, there were times I probably should’ve talked to somebody—my wife used to say I’d rather reorganize the garage than admit something was bothering me. And then I’d get caught up in work, driving all over for clients, making calls, all that noise… you just keep moving.

But no, not another episode that was treated by a counselor or psychiatrist or anything like that.
Have you had any episodes of depression before this one that felt similar to what you're experiencing now, but then got better on their own or with treatment?

I don’t think so… not like this.

I’ve had rough patches that eased up, sure—usually once whatever mess was going on passed. Like a bad stretch at work, money getting tight, family things… you know how one problem turns into five before lunch. But those didn’t feel the same as this does now.

So if you mean something that felt like this and then just lifted on its own, or because somebody treated it… no, I can’t really point to anything like that.
Did you have an episode of depression before this one that was treated and went away, but then came back?

No, I don’t think I had one like that—treated, went away, then came back. I mean, I’ve had ups and downs like anybody, and I’d tell myself it was just work or getting older or whatever. In sales you kind of learn to smile through a lot, even when you’re sitting in the car outside a client’s office wondering how you’re supposed to keep everything straight.

But no… if you mean something I actually got treated for and then it returned, I don’t have that history.
Did you consider the previous episodes of feeling down as the same kind of depression you are experiencing now?

I’m not sure I would’ve called them the same thing, no… I mean, at the time I just thought I was worn out or frustrated.

It’s funny, because I used to have days where I’d come home from driving around all day and just sit in the driveway for a minute before going inside, but then there was always dinner, bills, some customer calling about something that couldn’t possibly wait until morning. So I didn’t really stop and compare it, you know?

This now feels… I don’t know. I don’t think those earlier times were the same, but I may not be the best judge of it.
Did you have any earlier episodes of depression that were similar to this one and then went away before this episode started?

I don’t think so… I mean, not that I can clearly pick out.

There were times before where I felt low, sure, but it was usually tied up with other things—work being slow, customers changing their minds after I’d spent half the week chasing them, stuff at home piling up. And then I’d get busy again or something would shift, and I guess I’d just move on.

But similar to this? I don’t know. I wouldn’t say I had something like this that went away and then this started. At least not that I recognized that way.
Did you have any episodes of depression before this one that a doctor or therapist said would likely happen again?

No, I don’t think anyone ever told me that. I mean, I haven’t really had that kind of conversation before, where a doctor or therapist said, “This is probably going to come back.”

Most of the time, honestly, I just kept going. You know, in sales you get used to saying you’re fine because nobody wants to hear your whole life story when you’re supposed to be talking contracts or service plans. But no… not that I can remember. No one warned me about anything like that.
